classification.difficultyReason: Compare radius and diameter descriptions and justify equal circle size.

content.prompt: Calculate the circumferences of these two circles and show that they are the same size. Explain why.

spec.description: Equal displayed circles side by side: left radius 9 m extending upper-right; right near-vertical diameter 18 m.
spec.mathematics: Left r = 9 m; right d = 18 m.

answer.short: Both have circumference $18\pi\text{ m}$ and diameter $18\text{ m}$, so they are the same size.
answer.worked:
Circle 1:
$$\begin{align*}C_1&=2\pi r\\C_1&=2\times\pi\times9\\C_1&=18\pi\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
Circle 2:
$$\begin{align*}C_2&=\pi d\\C_2&=\pi\times18\\C_2&=18\pi\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
A radius of $9\text{ m}$ gives a diameter of $18\text{ m}$. Both circles therefore have the same diameter and circumference.
